```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4)
set.seed(1)
```

`dust2` returns model output as arrays, with state on the first dimension
and time on the last, and `monty` stores samples and trajectories the same
way. This package turns those arrays into long-format tibbles, with one row
per value, that can go straight into `ggplot2`.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(tidyodin)
library(odin2)
library(dust2)
library(monty)
library(ggplot2)
library(MetBrewer)
theme_set(theme_bw())
```

## A simulation

A stochastic SIR model that also tracks daily incidence, and can be
compared to case data:

```{r}
sir <- odin({
  update(S) <- S - n_SI
  update(I) <- I + n_SI - n_IR
  update(R) <- R + n_IR
  update(incidence) <- incidence + n_SI
  p_SI <- 1 - exp(-beta * I / N * dt)
  p_IR <- 1 - exp(-gamma * dt)
  n_SI <- Binomial(S, p_SI)
  n_IR <- Binomial(I, p_IR)
  initial(S) <- N - I0
  initial(I) <- I0
  initial(R) <- 0
  initial(incidence, zero_every = 1) <- 0
  N <- parameter(1000)
  I0 <- parameter(10)
  beta <- parameter(0.4)
  gamma <- parameter(0.1)
  cases <- data()
  cases ~ Poisson(incidence)
}, quiet = TRUE)
```

Run 30 particles and tidy the result. `tidy_simulation()` needs the system
and the times as well as the output, because the array does not record
either:

```{r}
sys <- dust_system_create(sir, list(), n_particles = 30, dt = 0.25)
dust_system_set_state_initial(sys)
t <- 0:60
y <- dust_system_simulate(sys, t)
dim(y)

sim <- tidy_simulation(y, sys, t)
sim
```

```{r}
nms_variable <- unique(sim$variable)
cols_variable <- met.brewer("Demuth", length(nms_variable))
names(cols_variable) <- nms_variable

ggplot(sim, aes(time, value, group = particle)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = variable), alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols_variable) +
  facet_wrap(vars(variable), scales = "free_y")
```

`summarise_trajectories()` collapses over particles (and draws and chains,
where present) for a ribbon plot:

```{r}
ggplot(summarise_trajectories(sim), aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = variable), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = median, colour = variable)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols_variable, aesthetics = c("fill", "colour")) +
  facet_wrap(vars(variable), scales = "free_y")
```

## Array variables

Variables with dimensions get one index column per dimension. `dims` names
those columns and `labels` turns an index into a labelled factor:

```{r}
sir_age <- odin({
  update(S[]) <- S[i] - n_SI[i]
  update(I[]) <- I[i] + n_SI[i] - n_IR[i]
  update(R[]) <- R[i] + n_IR[i]
  p_SI <- 1 - exp(-beta * sum(I) / sum(N) * dt)
  p_IR <- 1 - exp(-gamma * dt)
  n_SI[] <- Binomial(S[i], p_SI)
  n_IR[] <- Binomial(I[i], p_IR)
  initial(S[]) <- N[i] - 5
  initial(I[]) <- 5
  initial(R[]) <- 0
  N <- parameter()
  beta <- parameter(0.4)
  gamma <- parameter(0.1)
  n_age <- parameter(2)
  dim(S, I, R, n_SI, n_IR, N) <- n_age
}, quiet = TRUE)

sys <- dust_system_create(sir_age, list(N = c(300, 700)), n_particles = 10)
dust_system_set_state_initial(sys)
y <- dust_system_simulate(sys, t)

sim_age <- tidy_simulation(y, sys, t, dims = "age",
                           labels = list(age = c("children", "adults")))
sim_age

ggplot(sim_age, aes(time, value, colour = age,
                    group = interaction(age, particle))) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(vars(variable)) +
  scale_colour_met_d("Kandinsky")
```

## A fit

Fit the SIR model to some case data with a particle filter, saving the
trajectories and the final state of each sample:

```{r}
data <- data.frame(
  time = 1:20,
  cases = c(4, 8, 5, 12, 13, 19, 29, 34, 39, 42, 51, 44, 49, 38, 41, 33, 27,
            21, 22, 13))
filter <- dust_filter_create(sir, time_start = 0, data = data,
                             n_particles = 100, dt = 0.25)
packer <- monty_packer(c("beta", "gamma"), fixed = list(N = 1000, I0 = 10))
likelihood <- dust_likelihood_monty(filter, packer, save_trajectories = TRUE,
                                    save_state = TRUE)
prior <- monty_dsl({
  beta ~ Exponential(mean = 0.5)
  gamma ~ Exponential(mean = 0.2)
})
```

In this model `beta` and `gamma` are strongly correlated in the posterior,
so the random walk proposal is given a matching covariance (taken from a
short pilot run) to help the chains mix:

```{r}
vcv <- matrix(c(0.051, 0.040, 0.040, 0.035), 2, 2)
sampler <- monty_sampler_random_walk(vcv)
samples <- monty_sample(likelihood + prior, sampler, 3000,
                        initial = c(0.7, 0.45), n_chains = 3)
samples <- monty_samples_thin(samples, burnin = 1000, thinning_factor = 5)
```

Parameters, with chain and iteration recorded for trace plots:

```{r}
pars <- tidy_pars(samples)
pars

ggplot(pars, aes(iteration, value, colour = factor(chain))) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(vars(parameter), scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_met_d("Egypt") +
  labs(colour = "chain")
```

The fitted trajectories need the filter too, as the samples do not record
the names of the state variables or the times:

```{r}
fit <- tidy_trajectories(samples, filter, vars = "incidence")
fit

ggplot(fit, aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = sample), alpha = 0.03,
            colour = cols_variable["incidence"]) +
  geom_point(aes(y = cases), data = data) +
  labs(y = "incidence")
```

## Next steps

`vignette("parameter-sets")` shows how to run a model over many parameter
sets, for sensitivity analyses, projections from a fit and counterfactuals,
with output in this same format.
